messages:
jess (support): FYI just got an enterprise report — some users at Acme hit 403 after returning from GitHub/Google SSO. They see a state mismatch error in the UI.
rahul (eng): Can you paste the error text / Sentry link?
jess (support): Sentry auto post below. Customer says it happens if they click login twice quickly or use a mobile app then open in browser.
sentry-bot: New event: auth.oauth_callback failure (level: error)
  event.id: a1f3e7c4
  error: HTTP 403 - state_mismatch
  expected: "st_2026_abc"
  received: "st_2026_def"
john.doe (Acme): Confirmed — happens about 30% when user double-clicks the `Sign in with GitHub` button. If they hit back and retry, it usually clears.
olivia (devex): Interesting — sounds like a race between the PKCE/state generator and the session store. Are we overwriting the saved state on second click?
rahul (eng): Looking at the callback handler: we store {state, pkce_verifier} in session cookie then redirect to provider. If user opens a second auth flow, we generate a new state and set-cookie again. Callback compares incoming state to the last one in cookie => mismatch on the first flow returning. So race between two window flows.
lucas (oncall): Repro steps I used on Chrome mobile: 1) click Sign in 2) before redirect completes, tap Sign in again 3) get provider screen twice 4) complete first one => 403 on callback.
jess (support): Customer timeline: mobile in-app webview -> opens external browser -> they click login again while redirecting. So flow crosses contexts.
rahul (eng): Proposed mitigations: - debounce client button (short term) - make server support multiple outstanding states per session (store array, accept any recent N) - tie state to a transient ID in localStorage and send same id back to server so multiple flows can be correlated.
olivia (devex): Any security concerns accepting multiple outstanding states? Need TTL and limit to avoid CSRF windows.
rahul (eng): Agreed. Keep small TTL (60s), max 3 outstanding states, log any reuse. Also rotate pkce verifier per state but accept matching pair.
john.doe (Acme): For now their users need a quick workaround. What do we tell them?
jess (support): Suggested workaround: avoid double-clicks, update embedded webview to disable the button after first tap, or use the browser only flow. I sent that but customer wants a permanent fix.
rahul (eng): I'll open a small ticket for auth infra: allow up to 3 concurrent states per session + audit logs. Marking P2 since workaround exists, but for enterprise customers this should be P1 if affecting many orgs.
lucas (oncall): Adding note: mobile webviews sometimes clear cookies; consider using a transient localStorage key so flow remains consistent across context handoffs.
rahul (eng): Sentry event details attached: ```
HTTP 403 at /auth/callback
params: {provider: "github", state: "st_2026_def", code: "xxxx"}
cookie: session=eyJ... (last saved state: st_2026_abc)
session_id: sess-9b2f
```
jess (support): Escalation request: please review today and advise ETA. Customer on onboarding, 12 seats blocked.
rahul (eng): I'll triage now and post plan in ~2h. If anyone sees more repros, DM me the event IDs. :thumbsup:
